text:
devon: Quick sync - Prospect Helio Health wants a daytime low-latency chat (customer-facing) + nightly embedding ingestion. Theyneed a recommended GPU class, number of reserved GPUs for a 3-month commit, autoscale policy template, and a short reserved vs burst cost example for the execs. Can someone sketch?

marta: Quick clarifying q's: (1) peak concurrent chat qps? (2) typical chat token counts (median/p95)? (3) embeddings QPS and nightly batch size/dims?

sanjay: From the POC runs: chat peak ~220 qps sustained ~25-40m, median tokens ~40, p95 ~420. Embeddings steady ~120 qps at 1536 dims, nightly batch ~3M vectors over ~6h.

devon: They want tail latency <200ms for chat in production. Commit = reserved GPUs + burst credits for spikes.

marta: For <200ms p95: If they pick a 70B+ model -> H100-class recommended. For 20-33B a single A100-80GB can likely handle ~150 qps p95<200ms with tuned batching & KV cache. If they're using q4 quantized 33B chat, throughput improves ~2x.

sanjay: They plan open 33B q4. So assume 4-bit quantized for both chat and embeddings.

ops-bot: AUTOSCALE TEMPLATE (reserved-plus-burst):
```
min_replicas: reserved_capacity
scale_triggers:
  - queue_depth > 50 -> scale_up fast
  - cpu/gpu_util > 75% -> scale_up moderate
burst_pool: enabled (credit-limited, per-minute cap)
fallback: route to smaller quantized model variant
cooldown: 60s
```

marta: Ballpark sizing (scenario A - conservative):
- Chat (33B q4): A100-80 reserved sizing: ~1 GPU -> ~150 qps p95<200ms. For 220 peak recommend reserved=2, burst to 3.
- Embeddings (q4 1536d): 1 reserved GPU can sustain ~250-350 qps depending on batch. Nightly 3M over 6h ~= 140 qps sustained -> 1 GPU reserved fine, autoscale to 2 for ingest windows.
- Combined commit recommendation: reserved = 3 GPUs (2 chat pool, 1 embed pool) with burst credits allowing +50% capacity headroom.

marta: Scenario B (aggressive / cost-optimized): consolidate embedding and chat onto mixed pools with H100s and use higher burst limits; reserved 2 H100s used for both workloads with strict scheduling (requires operational guardrails).

devon: Finance asked for a simple monthly delta example: reserved vs hosted/pure PAYG. Can we throw a rough calc?

sanjay: Quick assumptions (placeholder numbers in deck later):
- Reserved GPU cost (monthly): $12k / GPU / mo (example)
- Hosted PAYG equivalent token/embedding unit rates: chat ~ $0.0008 / 1k tokens, embed ~ $0.0005 / vector (example)
- With our traffic, reserved 3 GPUs amortized yields ~40-60% lower per-request cost vs hosted at current sustained load. Exact breakeven depends on commit length and utilization.

marta: I'll build a 3-row sensitivity table (low / expected / high traffic) showing monthly cost reserved vs PAYG and breakeven utilization.

devon: Security/legal asks: Is reserved capacity shared or dedicated? KMS options for Private? SLA differences?

li-legal: For enterprise commits we offer Dedicated (customer-isolated tenancy) or Private (VPC + on-prem option). KMS integration available for Private; we'll need their SOC docs + RA details. I'll start the security questionnaire and list required artifacts. Need answers in 48h for the legal team to approve contract.

devon: Can we include KV warmup / preheat guidance? Theyworry about cold-start tail latency.

marta: Yes. Recommendation: KV preheat 30-45m before business-critical windows. Warmup script pattern (example):
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
    -d '{"prompt":"seed prompt"}' &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
Also: populate prefix cache with top-k user prompts and ramp traffic gradually.

sanjay: Runbook notes: autoscale cooldown 60s, queue-depth-based throttling to avoid cascading latency. Canary fallback to a smaller quantized model if p95 spikes > target for N consecutive intervals.

devon: Action items: marta -> sizing + cost spreadsheet (conservative & aggressive scenarios). sanjay -> autoscale config + preheat/runbook + smoke-test plan. li-legal -> first-pass questionnaire answers + artifacts list. I'll package and send to Helio and schedule a 1-hr tech walkthrough in 48h.

marta: On it. I'll attach the spreadsheet and include assumptions. :thumbsup:

sanjay: I'll add a short smoke test that runs the warmup script and measures p50/p95 over 30m.

li-legal: I'll post the questionnaire draft and docs list by EOD tomorrow.

devon: Thanks team. I'll email the customer summary and confirm the walkthrough.
